question: Explain the requirements for generating an e-way bill under the CGST Rules, 2017 and the consequences of transporting goods without the prescribed documents.

points.label: When an e-way bill is required
points.description: A registered person who causes movement of goods of a consignment value above the prescribed limit, whether for a supply, for reasons other than supply (such as sending goods for job work) or because of an inward supply from an unregistered person, must furnish the details electronically before the movement starts; this applies to inter-State and intra-State movement.

points.label: Part A and Part B
points.description: Part A carries the invoice or document details, recipient, place of delivery, value and reason for transport; Part B carries the vehicle or transport document details. It is generated by the consignor or consignee, or by the transporter where they have not done so, and a unique e-way bill number is made available to the supplier, recipient and transporter.
points.basis: CGST Rules, 2017, rule 138 (generation of e-way bill and form EWB-01)

points.label: Validity, extension and cancellation
points.description: Validity depends on the distance to be covered, counted from generation of Part B, and can be extended before expiry where goods cannot reach in time for exceptional reasons; an e-way bill may be cancelled within 24 hours of generation if goods are not transported or not as per the details, unless it has been verified in transit.

points.label: Cases where it is not needed
points.description: No e-way bill is needed in specified cases, such as goods moved by a non-motorised conveyance, goods moved from a port, airport or land customs station to an inland container depot or container freight station for customs clearance, and goods under customs supervision or seal.

points.label: Consequences of moving goods without documents
points.description: The person in charge of the conveyance must carry the prescribed documents and e-way bill, and officers may intercept and verify them; goods and the conveyance moved in contravention may be detained or seized and released on payment of the penalty provided, with confiscation possible where there is intent to evade tax.
points.basis: CGST Act, 2017, sections 68, 129 and 130; CGST Rules, 2017, rule 138A
